summary: Created a 9-phase consumer-side implementation plan covering all 5 WORK items across 8 source-store files (orchestrate-predispatch-review.sh is read-only for this task). Phases are ordered so each ends at a verifiable, committable green state, with deploy deliberately confined to the final phase because redeploying rewrites the running orchestrator's own skill and command definitions. The plan makes two binding decisions the research left open: --allow-scope-collision bypasses cross_batch ONLY (never in_batch, because in_batch means two live co-dispatched agents editing the same files and already has a free bounded-retry remedy), and orchestrate-dry-run-report.sh plus the hard twin's stale schema-v4 mention are confirmed in scope.

artifacts.summary: 9-phase consumer-side threading plan for all 5 WORK items across 8 source-store files, with two binding design decisions and a final deploy/verify phase.

decisions_made: D1: --allow-scope-collision bypasses cross_batch file_scope_collision ONLY, never in_batch. Rejected the research report's both-scopes recommendation: in_batch means the colliding task is a live co-dispatched agent in this same cycle (concurrent-write corruption hazard) and already has a zero-cost bounded remedy via multi-task-operations.md's Tier 1 auto-sequence second pass; only cross_batch's excluded-from-run outcome is legitimate override territory. Consequence: the flag's help text and every bypass notice must say 'cross-batch' explicitly so the unqualified name does not mislead.

D2: orchestrate-dry-run-report.sh IS in scope for WORK 1 (the research flagged this as inferred rather than asserted). It is in the declared file_scope, is one of the schema doc's four named defer_reason-branching consumers, and has the identical idle_overlap_advisory rendering gap. Phase 6 covers it as its own committable phase.

D3: skill-orchestrate-hard/SKILL.md's stale 'schema v4' mention is swept to v5 in the same pass as the two literal 'v3' files WORK 5 names, per the co-maintenance mandate requiring the twins to agree with each other and with the live predicate.

D4: task-lock.md and multi-task-operations.md are in the declared file_scope and get a bounded treatment rather than silence. D1's new cross_batch/in_batch asymmetry lands on multi-task-operations.md's Tier 1 auto-sequence discussion and must be cross-referenced there; task-lock.md is edited only if it contradicts D1, otherwise closed with a Reasoned Exclusions record.

Phase sequencing: phases 2, 3, and 4 all edit the same cross_batch warning bullet regions and are therefore strictly sequential (waves 2-4) rather than parallel, to prevent churn. Phases 1, 6, and 7 are mutually independent and form wave 1.
